# skill: product-naming

Use when naming a product, shop, app or brand

# Naming a product

> **The one rule:** a good name is one a person **types correctly the first time, after hearing it once.**
> Deeper meaning can come later, but if people misspell the name, customers cannot find you.

## When to use this skill

- Naming a product, shop, service, app, brand, module or internal project
- A name exists but feels dated, long or the same as someone else's
- There are several products and the names should form one family
- You must choose from a brainstormed list of names and cannot decide

Not for: logo, colours, brand typography → `graphic-design` · naming document files → `document-naming` · naming tables and columns → `database-design` · naming endpoints → `api-conventions`

---

## 1 · Six tests that cut a name at once

Test before you think further. If a name fails any one, cut it. Do not feel sorry.

| # | Test | Fails when |
|:--:|---|---|
| 1 | **Phone test**: say the name to someone over the phone. Do they type it correctly? | You have to spell it out |
| 2 | **Length** | More than 3 syllables, or more than 12 letters |
| 3 | **Domain and handle** | `.com` and `.co` are both taken and no social handle is free anywhere |
| 4 | **Collision with what exists** | A product, shop or service in the same category has the same or a very close name |
| 5 | **Meaning in other languages** | It means something bad in a language your customers speak |
| 6 | **Thai speakers can pronounce it** | It has a consonant cluster Thai speakers avoid, or ends in a sound that gets swallowed |

**Also cut:** a number in the name (`App360` · `Pro24` go stale when the version changes) · 3 or more words (nobody says the whole thing, so it gets shortened until it cannot be recognised).

> **People often forget test 6.** If the name has `th`, `v` or `z` at the end of a word, or a cluster like `str-` or `spl-`,
> Thai speakers will pronounce it off and type what they heard.

---

## 2 · Nine formulas for producing names

Do not sit and think in the air. Walk through the formulas one at a time, come up with 5–10 names per formula, then select.

| # | Formula | Method | Example |
|:--:|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Real word, cut the end** | Take an English word and drop the last syllable | `figure` → **Figma** · `velocity` → **Velo** |
| 2 | **2 words collided** | Cut the head and tail of 2 words and join them | `fold`+`drop` → **Foldrop** · `data`+`dog` → **Datadog** |
| 3 | **Word + suffix** | Add `-io` `-ly` `-ify` `-o` `-a` `-ex` | `home`+`ify` → **Homify** · `aurum`+`io` → **Aurio** |
| 4 | **Latin/Greek root** | Find the root word for what it does, then shorten it | `lumen` → **Lumo** · `nexus` → **Nexa** |
| 5 | **Family letters** | A word for the function + a family ending | **TradeXI · TelXI · DockXI · SoundXI** |
| 6 | **Short meaningless word** | 4–5 letters, consonant-vowel-consonant, readable at once | **Quix · Zeno · Riva · Volt** |
| 7 | **Real word borrowed across contexts** | An ordinary word unrelated to the work that gives the right feeling | **Slack · Notion · Arc · Linear** |
| 8 | **2 syllables that read smoothly** | 2 short real words side by side | **Speak Go · Cash App** |
| 9 | **2 whole unrelated words** | Join 2 real words that relate neither to the product nor to each other into one word | **Tailscale · Snowflake · Firebase · Basecamp** |

**The formulas that give the most "cool + clean" names** are 1 · 4 · 6, because they give short names with no literal meaning that are easy to remember.
**Formula 7 gives names that look grown-up**, but its domains are the hardest to find.

**Letters that feel modern:** start with `x` `z` `q` `v`, or end with `-o` `-a` `-ix` `-ex`.
**Letters that look dated:** ending with `-soft` `-tech` `-sys` `-pro` `-plus` `-max`.

---

**Formula 9 in depth:** take 2 whole real words (cut nothing) that relate neither to the product nor to each other, and put them side by side · at most 3 syllables in total · the first word concrete · read every pair aloud before choosing → reasons, rules and the A/B word pools for pairing are in [`references/formula-9-deep-dive.md`](references/formula-9-deep-dive.md). Open it when you use formula 9.

## 3 · Giving the name a meaning

A short, modern name does not have to be meaningless, because meaning can arrive 2 ways.

| Way | Formulas that give it | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Built in from birth** | 4 Latin/Greek roots · 7 real words borrowed across contexts | `Aurio` from *aurum*, gold · `Anchor`, stability |
| **Added later** | 6 short meaningless words | `Quix` is chosen first, then tied to speed |

**Rule for meaning:** find the root from **what the user gets**, not from what the system does.
For example, for a gold inventory system, use the root "gold", not the root "warehouse".

**Test:** can you write the meaning in **1 line**?
"Aurio: from Latin aurum, meaning gold." That is all. If it takes more than 1 sentence to explain, the meaning is too weak.

**Thinking libraries:** a table of Latin/Greek roots that work in practice (light · gold · connect · time · protect and others) and a table of real words borrowed across contexts, grouped by feeling (fast · stable · clear · orderly · connected · guiding · quiet) → [`references/meaning-libraries.md`](references/meaning-libraries.md). Open it when you use formula 4 or 7. Real words are the hardest to find domains for, so keep a fallback (`arc.app` · `getprism.com`).

**The story:** short, memorable, easy to retell (not a chain of initials, and not the family dog's name) → good and bad examples in `references/meaning-libraries.md`

**Write the meaning into the brand document** on the day you pick the name, not when someone asks.
That way the sales team tells it the same way every time.

---

## 4 · Name families, when there are several products

Pick one pattern and use it for the whole family.

| Pattern | Looks like | Good | Bad |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Same ending** | `TradeXI` `TelXI` `DockXI` | You know at once they share a house, and new names are easy to make | If one name is damaged, the whole family suffers |
| **Same prefix** | `QuixChat` `QuixFlow` | The parent brand stands out | Every name gets longer |
| **Independent** | `Aurio` `Homify` `Foldrop` | Each one sells itself and can be sold separately | You must build a new brand for each |

**How to choose:** if you sell them as a bundle, use one family. If you might sell them separately or sell the business later, make them independent.

> **Write the family's naming rules down in a document**, together with the rule for naming the next one.
> Otherwise the 5th name breaks the pattern and the whole set looks messy.

---

## 5 · Check what is available before you fall in love

**Check when 5 names are left, not when 1 is left.** If you love a name and then learn you cannot use it, it hurts more.

| Check what | Where | Fails when |
|---|---|---|
| Domain | Domain registrar | `.com` and `.co` are taken and no fallback is left |
| Thai trademark | กรมทรัพย์สินทางปัญญา (Department of Intellectual Property) | A registration exists in our goods or services category |
| International trademark | WIPO database | Same as above, if you will sell abroad |
| Package name (if software) | npm · PyPI · NuGet | Already used in the ecosystem you will publish to |
| App store name (if an app) | App Store · Play Store | An app with the same name exists in the same category |
| Social handles | X · Instagram · Facebook · TikTok · GitHub · LINE | None is free |
| Plain search | Search engine | The first page is full of other people's results |

**Decision rule:** you must get the main domain, at least half the handles must be free, and
there must be no trademark collision in our category. These 3 have no exceptions.

---

## 6 · Sound and typing in the Thai context

| Topic | Rule |
|---|---|
| Thai customers will certainly write the name in Thai | Try writing it yourself first, for example `Aurio` as "ออริโอ", and see if it reads smoothly |
| Choose 1 official Thai form | Follow the transliteration rules of the Royal Society of Thailand (ราชบัณฑิตยสภา) with no tone marks (ซอฟต์แวร์, not ซ้อฟต์แว่ร์) · record it in the brand kit · keep other forms that customers actually type as search keywords, not for the work itself |
| Sounds Thai speakers swallow | `-th` `-v` `-s` at the end of a word vanish almost every time |
| Clusters they avoid | `str-` `spl-` `thr-` |
| Names easy to mistype on a Thai keyboard | Avoid letters so close together that they can swap |
| Length when written in Thai | No more than 5 Thai syllables |

**Real test:** say the name to 3 Thai speakers over the phone and have them type it in LINE and send it back.
If even 1 person types it differently, the name fails.

---

## 7 · Five tests before the final decision

| # | Test | Passes when |
|:--:|---|---|
| 1 | Write it in a real sentence | "ลองใช้ ___ ดูสิ" (Thai for "try ___") sounds natural |
| 2 | Write it next to the category word | "___ — ระบบจัดการคลังทอง" (Thai for "___, a gold inventory system") reads and makes sense |
| 3 | Shrink it to an icon | The first letter or 2 can become a symbol |
| 4 | Survives when the scope grows | A name with the word "gold" breaks the day you also sell silver |
| 5 | Resists teasing | Try making up jokes about your own name. If they come too easily, beware |

**Test 4 matters most for anything that will keep growing.** A meaningless name is safer in the long run.

## Related skills

Logo, colours, typography → `graphic-design` · same product already exists under this name → `prior-art-review` · names in documents → `document-naming` · feature terms inside the product → `i18n-and-locale` · presenting the shortlist → `presentation-design`. A shortlist table you can fill in right away → `assets/name-shortlist.md`


## reference: formula-9-deep-dive.md

# Formula 9 in depth

Open this when you generate names with formula 9.

## The pattern that makes a name look coolest without inventing a word

`Tailscale` = *tail* + *scale*. Neither word has anything to do with private networks, and the two words have nothing to do with each other either.

| How it differs from formula 2 | |
|---|---|
| Formula 2 | **Cuts** syllables before joining, such as `fold`+`drop` → Foldrop, so the result is not a real word |
| Formula 9 | **Cuts nothing.** Put 2 whole real words side by side |

**Why it works**

| Reason | |
|---|---|
| Easy to remember | The listener already knows both words, so there is no new spelling to learn |
| Unique | Nothing forces these words together, so nobody has paired them before |
| Domains are easier to find | Usually easier than a single word, but still check them as in section 5 of `SKILL.md` |
| Passes the phone test | The listener types it correctly at once, because the words are familiar |

**Rules for this formula**

- Total of at most **3 syllables**: `Tailscale` 2 · `Basecamp` 2 · `Snowflake` 2
- **The first word should be concrete**, something you can picture (tail, snow, fire, base, bit, black, cloud)
- Do not let the pair describe the product. If it explains the product, it becomes a dated name like `DataSync`
- **The combined meaning must not come out odd.** Read it aloud and picture it first
- Spellings must not collide into something hard to read. Avoid a first word that ends with the same letter the second word starts with

**How to generate** — build 2 separate pools, then pair at random and read every pair aloud

| Pool A: concrete | Pool B: structure/measure |
|---|---|
| tail · snow · fire · bit · black · cloud · iron · salt · moon · north · glass · pine | scale · flake · base · bucket · camp · bird · flare · stack · frame · gate · port · line |

Example pairs: `Saltframe` · `Pinegate` · `Moonstack` · `Ironport` · `Glassline`

> **Meaning can be added fully afterward** (see item 3). `Tailscale` had no meaning at the start,
> but after some use, people tied it to the idea of a network that can scale.


## reference: meaning-libraries.md

# Libraries for developing a name's meaning

Contents: Latin/Greek root library → real words borrowed across contexts → good and bad stories

## Latin/Greek roots that work in practice

| Meaning | Root | Resulting names |
|---|---|---|
| light · clarity | *lux · lumen* | Lumo · Lumen · Lucent |
| gold · valuable | *aurum* | Aurio · Aura |
| connect | *nexus · syn-* | Nexa · Syno · Nexo |
| power · electricity | *volta · vis* | Volta · Vira |
| circle · world | *orbis · kyklos* | Orbis · Kyklo |
| time · rhythm | *tempus · chronos · kairos* | Tempo · Chrono · Kairo |
| flow · move | *fluxus · kinesis* | Flux · Kinet |
| sound | *sonus · vox* | Sona · Voxa |
| store · chest | *arca* | Arca · Arka |
| protect · shield | *aegis · scutum* | Aegis · Scuto |
| care · look after | *cura* | Cura · Curo |
| beginning | *arche* | Arka · Archo |
| form | *morphe* | Morpho · Forma |
| word · language | *lexis · verbum* | Lexi · Verba |
| look · inspect | *specto* | Specta · Scopo |
| new | *nova* | Nova · Novo |
| true | *veritas* | Vera · Verio |
| work · output | *opus* | Opus · Opero |
| port · door | *portus · porta* | Porta · Portio |

## Real words borrowed across contexts, grouped by feeling

| Feeling | Words |
|---|---|
| fast · agile | Arc · Bolt · Dash · Swift · Rush · Skim |
| stable · safe | Anchor · Vault · Keel · Bastion · Forge · Bedrock |
| clear · visible | Prism · Lens · Beacon · Signal · Facet |
| orderly | Grid · Frame · Ledger · Atlas · Index · Stack |
| connected | Bridge · Relay · Mesh · Loom · Thread · Weave |
| guiding | Compass · Pilot · Helm · North · Trail |
| quiet · smooth | Slate · Quill · Linen · Drift · Still |

> Warning: **real words are the hardest to find domains for**, so prepare a fallback, such as adding a category word (`arc.app`, `getprism.com`)
> or using another short domain style.

## Good and bad stories

| | Example |
|---|---|
| ✓ Good | "Aegis is the shield of Zeus. This system exists to protect." Short, memorable, easy to retell |
| ✗ Bad | "A stands for Advanced, U for Unified, R for Realtime…" Nobody remembers it |
| ✗ Bad | "The name comes from the family dog's name." A personal meaning, so customers feel nothing |

# skill: project-bootstrap

Use when starting a repository or setting up a new machine

# Project bootstrap

> **The one rule:** someone who has never seen this project must be able to run it within **30 minutes**,
> reading only `README.md` and asking nobody.

## When to use this skill

Starting a new repository · a newcomer needs half a day before the project runs · a pull request shows a whole-file diff because formatters disagree · nobody knows where the documents are

Not for: build and deploy pipeline → `cicd-and-release` · per-environment settings and secrets → `config-and-secrets` · choosing an architecture → `architecture-patterns` · test framework → `testing-standards` · naming documents → `document-naming`

---

## 1 · Folder layout

**The root (the folder the user opens) follows `project-doc-set` item 1, layout B.** The root tree, the ecosystem layout and the SuperUser file locations (`.claude/superuser/`) are defined there and only there. Code lives in `<project-name>/`. Its inner layout is:

Inside `<project-name>/` (lowercase project name, words joined by `-`): `README.md` (item 2) · `CHANGELOG.md` · `ARCHITECTURE.md` · `CONTRIBUTING.md` · `LICENSE` (these 3 only when the conditions in `references/readme-skeleton.md` section 2 apply) · `.env.example` (only when the project really reads environment variables · `config-and-secrets`) · `.editorconfig` · `.gitattributes` · `.gitignore` (build output · secrets · `_to_delete/`) · `src/` (unit tests sit beside the code files · `readable-code` item 7) · `tests/` (integration · e2e only, or stacks whose tools require it, see "Exceptions by stack" below) · `scripts/` (setup · seed · migrate). The annotated tree is in [`references/code-folder.md`](references/code-folder.md). ADRs (architecture decision records) and runbooks live in `docs/` at the root, not in the code folder (`project-doc-set` item 1).

**Extensions and sub-programs go in `extension/`.** When the app ships add-ons or small companion programs that belong to it (a browser extension · an IDE or app plugin · a hook client or CLI · an SDK · a tray helper · a worker that cannot run alone), put each one in `<project-name>/extension/<name>/`, named lowercase with `-` (`extension/chrome/` · `extension/hook-client/` · `extension/sdk-python/`). The folder is always named `extension/` (never `plugins/` `addons/` `packages/` `tools/`), so whoever opens the repo sees the main app first and every add-on in one place. Each `extension/<name>/` has its own README (what it extends · how to build and run · how it talks to the main app) and its own build and tests in its own stack's layout; CI builds and tests every one, and a workspace tool (pnpm · npm · Cargo · .NET solution) lists `extension/*`. The main app's code stays in `src/` (or the stack's folder). Create `extension/` when the first add-on is written, not in advance. An add-on that grows its own doc set (SRS · mockup · its own release cycle) is a sub-project: move it to `ecosystem/` per `project-doc-set` item 1.

**Code folder name.** Take the project folder name, lowercase it, and turn each run of spaces and punctuation into a single `-`:
`Lumio - Light Meter/` → `lumio-light-meter/`
Run every build, test and run command from inside this folder. In languages that force a package-name format (Dart `name:` in pubspec · Python package), keep naming the package by the language's rules, because this rule governs only the folder name.

**Root rules (the top level of the project folder):**
- Hold only what is in the `project-doc-set` item 1 layout. Exceptions are declared in the project's README. README, CHANGELOG and config files live in the repo. Received `.docx`/`.xlsx` files go in `ref/`. Ones we write go in `docs/`.
- **Temporary files never live at the root.** If a temp file an agent created lands at the root, move it into `_to_delete/` at once.
- If a build leaves a stray folder at the root (such as an empty `build/` or `lib/` after moving the code), a tool cache still remembers the old path. Clear the cache (`flutter clean` · delete `obj/`) and build again.
- Folder and file names in the repo are lowercase with hyphens and no spaces. **The exception is a language with its own convention.** Follow that language.

**Exceptions by stack.** The code folder name, the test folder and the file names follow what the language's tools expect. Do not force `src/`. Test files normally sit beside the code files; use a separate test folder only for stacks whose tools require one (.NET: `tests/` with a separate test `.csproj` · Dart / Flutter: `lib/`, `test/` and `integration_test/` required). The full per-stack table is in [`references/code-folder.md`](references/code-folder.md). When another skill writes `tests/` or `test/`, read it as "the test folder of that stack". Pick one name and use it across the whole repo.

**Layout A** (use only when the user asks · this item owns the layout). Add `<project-name>/docs/` inside the code folder, as plain markdown. The inner layout matches the `docs/` of layout B (`README.md` index · `decisions/ADR-NNNN-<slug>.md` · `runbook-<topic>.md` · `research/`). It has no `.docx` or PNG deliverables. The rest of the root still follows the `project-doc-set` item 1 layout, without a `docs/` at the root.

**`docs/README.md` is an index, not content:**

Template → `assets/starter-files.md` (columns: document · read when · owner · last updated)

---

## 2 · README — broad outline, then survey the project before choosing sections

READMEs differ from job to job. A web app · library · CLI (Command-Line Interface) · mobile app · monorepo · infra or script project needs different sections and commands. So work in 3 layers:

**Layer 1 · Broad outline (fixed).** The README must answer these questions for a newcomer, in the order they need them:
What is this and who uses it → what must be on the machine → install and run → configure → common commands (test) → project structure → architecture → build → deploy → troubleshooting → contributing → contact → license
Drop any question the project has nothing for. The exception is "configure", which must say there are no external settings.

**Layer 2 · Survey before writing (every time).** Record the results in `_to_delete/readme-survey.md` and use them to decide layer 3.
1. **Read the project:** package manifest files (`package.json` · `*.csproj` · `pyproject.toml` · `pubspec.yaml` and so on) · version-pin files · `Dockerfile` / `compose` · CI (Continuous Integration) files · `Makefile` / scripts · `.env.example` · top-level folders → this gives the project type, stack, the commands that really exist and the system's components (`code-orientation` if the code is large).
2. **Search the official documentation for that stack** (`research-with-sources`): install, run, test and build commands, and which files to commit, for the version the project uses. Never put commands from memory or from the fallback table into the README without checking them.
3. **Look at 2–3 READMEs of well-known projects of the same type** (search by project type + stack) to see which extra sections readers in that field expect. For example, a library has code samples and a table of supported versions · a CLI has command options · infra has what to prepare in the cloud account · a mobile app has flavors and how to sign the app.
4. If search is impossible (no internet), use the layer 3 fallback tables and mark each unchecked command `(รอยืนยัน)` (awaiting confirmation).

**Layer 3 · Choose sections and commands.** Arrange the sections from layer 1 plus the extra sections found in step 3. Take commands from steps 1–2. The full table (what each section answers · how long it should be · where to move it when too long) is in [`references/readme-skeleton.md`](references/readme-skeleton.md). It is a fallback and a length guide, not a list that must be complete.

- **The README holds only what a newcomer uses in the first 30 minutes.** Move anything longer to `ARCHITECTURE.md` · `CONTRIBUTING.md` · `docs/runbook-deploy.md` and link back (see the "split into other files" table and the `ARCHITECTURE.md` template in the same file).
- **Fallback tables by language** (Node · .NET · Python · Java · Go · Flutter · Rust · Laravel) → [`references/readme-by-stack.md`](references/readme-by-stack.md). Use them as the starting point for the layer 2 step 2 search. For a stack not in the tables, search the official documentation directly.
- Copy-ready templates (Node · Flutter / Android) → `assets/starter-files.md`. An app with no DB or Docker must still list everything needed on the machine.

> **Every command must have been run on a clean machine.** Most READMEs are wrong because the author
> already has everything on their own machine and cannot see the missing steps.
>
> **1 install command, 1 run command.** If there are 12 steps, write them as `scripts/setup.sh`.

---

## 3 · CHANGELOG

Use the Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 format. Order the headings in each version as follows and drop headings with no items: **เปลี่ยนที่ทำให้ของเดิมพัง** (breaking changes; our own addition, always on top) · เพิ่ม · เปลี่ยน · จะเลิกใช้ · เอาออก · แก้ · ความปลอดภัย. Keep `[ยังไม่ปล่อย]` (unreleased) at the top at all times. Put the newest version first. Write dates as `YYYY-MM-DD`. The full example is in [`references/changelog-examples.md`](references/changelog-examples.md).

**Is a CHANGELOG needed?**

| Situation | CHANGELOG |
|---|---|
| Delivered to a customer, with a UAT (user acceptance testing) round or a version number | Required — the customer and the acceptance reviewer see what this round delivers |
| Others call it (API · library · app with users) | Required — they learn whether they must change anything on their side |
| Prototype · personal script · solo work with no release rounds | Not needed — `git log` is enough · write the reason in the README |

**Write for the people who use the product.** 1 item per line, stating the result the user sees, not a commit list, file names or ticket numbers. Leave out invisible work unless it can be felt. "เปลี่ยนที่ทำให้ของเดิมพัง" is always on top. The full rules and the wrong → right examples are in [`references/changelog-examples.md`](references/changelog-examples.md).
- For version numbers and bump rules, see `cicd-and-release`.

---

## 4 · Formatters and linters — end the style arguments

- `.editorconfig` (indentation · line endings · encoding) for every language · template with `.gitattributes` → `assets/starter-files.md`
- The formatter fixes style on save (Prettier · dotnet format · black/ruff · `dart format`). The linter catches only real mistakes (ESLint · .NET analyzers · ruff · `flutter analyze`).
- Set `end_of_line = lf` and `.gitattributes` `* text=auto eol=lf`. Otherwise a team mixing Windows with other systems gets pull requests that diff the whole file.
- **The formatter decides for people.** Any setting is fine, but the whole team must use the same one.
- Have CI check it too, instead of trusting that everyone set up their machine the same way.
- When turning it on in an old project, format the whole repo in **one commit with nothing else in it**,
  then add that commit to `.git-blame-ignore-revs`.

---

## 5 · Dependencies

- **Always commit the lock file**, and install on CI with a command that follows the lock (`npm ci` · `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile`). Otherwise each day's build gets a different set.
- Check for vulnerabilities in the pipeline (`cicd-and-release`). Update on a schedule: patch monthly, minor quarterly, not only when something breaks.
- A new dependency needs a reason in the pull request (`lazy-coding`).

**Before adding a library, ask 3 questions:** can the language's standard library do it, is the project still alive, and
does the license allow use in work that is sold (see `prior-art-review`)?

---

## 6 · Checklist when opening a new project

Tick `[x]` only for items you **ran or opened in this round**. For an item not yet built or run, write `[ ]` and say what is pending. For an item that does not apply to this project, write `N/A — <reason>`.

- [ ] `README.md` answers the layer 1 questions the project has content for · sections and commands come from the layer 2 survey results (`_to_delete/readme-survey.md` exists) · commands have been run on a clean machine
- [ ] The root matches the layout in `project-doc-set` item 1 (repo named as the lowercase project name joined by `-` · an ecosystem uses `ecosystem/`) and has no temp files or `.docx` at the root
- [ ] Add-ons and sub-programs of the app live in `<project-name>/extension/<name>/`, each with its own README and a CI build, or `N/A` when the app has none
- [ ] `.env.example` lists every value with comments. If the project reads no environment variables at all (for example an offline mobile app), do not create it, but write "ไม่มีค่าตั้งภายนอก" (no external settings) in the README
- [ ] `.editorconfig` · `.gitattributes` · formatter · linter are set up, and CI checks them
- [ ] `.gitignore` covers `.env` · build folders · `_to_delete/` · Android: `key.properties` · `*.jks` · `*.keystore`
- [ ] `docs/README.md` is an index, with an owner for each document
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` has an "ยังไม่ปล่อย" heading waiting
- [ ] At least 1 test runs and passes, to prove the layout works
- [ ] `main` is protected and needs a pull request and CI. A repo with no remote, or a solo repo, may skip this, but must write the reason in the README and run tests and the linter before each commit instead.
- [ ] **Have someone who did not set up the project follow the README, and time them**

---
## References

## reference: changelog-examples.md

# CHANGELOG — examples

Read this when writing a CHANGELOG for the first time or reviewing one. The rules are in `SKILL.md` item 3. The blank template is in `assets/starter-files.md`. The sample below is Thai because the CHANGELOG itself is written for Thai users.

```markdown
# Changelog

## [ยังไม่ปล่อย]
### เพิ่ม
- ส่งออกรายงานเป็น Excel

## [1.2.0] — 2026-09-25
### เปลี่ยนที่ทำให้ของเดิมพัง
- `GET /orders` คืน `data` แทนอาเรย์ตรง ๆ — ดู API-CONVENTIONS.md
### เพิ่ม
- แจ้งเตือนทาง LINE
### จะเลิกใช้
- ส่งออกรายงานเป็น CSV จะเอาออกในรุ่น 2.0 — ใช้ Excel แทน
### แก้
- ยอดรวมปัดเศษผิดเมื่อมีส่วนลด
### ความปลอดภัย
- ผู้ใช้ที่ถูกปิดบัญชีเปิดลิงก์ใบเสร็จเก่าไม่ได้แล้ว

## [1.1.1] — 2026-09-10 [ถอน]
```

## Headings and version numbers

| Heading (Keep a Changelog) | Use for | Version part to bump (Semantic Versioning) |
|---|---|---|
| เปลี่ยนที่ทำให้ของเดิมพัง (breaking changes; our own addition) | Users or calling systems must change something on their side | MAJOR · in the `0.y.z` range, MINOR is allowed |
| เพิ่ม (Added) | New capability | MINOR |
| เปลี่ยน (Changed) | Existing behavior works differently but does not break | MINOR |
| จะเลิกใช้ (Deprecated) | Still works but will be removed · name the removal version and the replacement | MINOR |
| เอาออก (Removed) | Already removed | MAJOR |
| แก้ (Fixed) | Bugs | PATCH |
| ความปลอดภัย (Security) | Vulnerabilities already closed · do not describe how to attack | PATCH, or by size |

The version-bump column is this skill's own proposal. Semantic Versioning says only this: MAJOR = incompatible with the old version · MINOR = backward-compatible additions or deprecation notices · PATCH = backward-compatible bug fixes.

If a released version must be pulled because of a serious bug or vulnerability, append `[ถอน]` to the version heading (Keep a Changelog uses `[YANKED]`). Do not delete that version. Sources: [Keep a Changelog 1.1.0](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) · [Semantic Versioning 2.0.0](https://semver.org/) · opened 2026-11-07

Write what the user sees, not a list of commits:

| ✗ | ✓ |
|---|---|
| `- fix(items): change > to >= in withdraw() (#42)` | `- เบิกของเท่ากับจำนวนที่เหลือพอดีได้แล้ว` |
| `- refactor lowStockReport to read movements once` | `- รายงานของใกล้หมดเปิดได้ในไม่ถึง 1 วินาที (เดิม 50 วินาที)` |

## Writing rules (full version)

- Write for the **people who use the product**. Do not paste the commit list.
- 1 item = 1 line. Say what the user gains or sees change, not which file changed.
- Leave out file names, function names and ticket numbers, unless the reader is a developer who calls that API.
- Leave out work the user cannot see, such as code restructuring, new tests or CI fixes. The exception is a speed or stability gain big enough to feel. Then write it as the result ("รายงานของใกล้หมดเปิดได้ในไม่ถึง 1 วินาที").
- Within each heading, put the items that affect users most at the top. Drop any heading that has no items.
- The heading "เปลี่ยนที่ทำให้ของเดิมพัง" must always sit at the **top** of that version. Every deprecation, removal and breaking change must be listed, even a small one.


## reference: code-folder.md

# Code folder layout — full tree

The rules are in `SKILL.md` item 1. The root tree is in `project-doc-set` item 1. ADRs (architecture decision records) and runbooks live in `docs/` at the root, not here.

```
<project-name>/          ← lowercase project name, words joined by `-`
  README.md              ← item 2 · broad outline + survey the project before choosing sections
  CHANGELOG.md           ← what changed in each version
  ARCHITECTURE.md        ← code map · add it when the README tree passes 15 lines or the system has many parts (references/readme-skeleton.md)
  CONTRIBUTING.md        ← add it when the contributing section in the README passes 5 lines
  LICENSE                ← public repo, or the contract requires it
  .env.example           ← every required value (see config-and-secrets) · only when the project really reads environment variables
  .editorconfig          ← item 4
  .gitattributes
  .gitignore             ← build output · secrets · `_to_delete/`
  src/                   ← the real code (or the layout the stack expects, per `SKILL.md` item 1)
  tests/                 ← required in .NET · Flutter (`test/`) · Node and Python keep only integration and e2e here (unit tests sit beside the code files) — the stack table is at the end of this file
  scripts/               ← setup, seed, migrate — scripts a person has to run
  extension/             ← add-ons and sub-programs of this app, 1 folder each: browser extension · plugin · CLI · hook client · SDK (`SKILL.md` item 1) · only when one exists
    <name>/              ← own README · own build and tests in that stack's layout
```

## Exceptions by stack

**Exceptions by stack.** The code folder name, the test folder and the file names in the repo follow what the language's tools expect.
Do not force `src/`. Test files normally sit beside the code files. Use a separate test folder only for stacks whose tools require one (the cells marked **required**):

| Stack | Code | Tests | File names |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node | `src/` | Unit tests beside the code files (`*.test.ts`) · integration and e2e in `tests/` | `kebab-case` |
| .NET | `src/` | `tests/` **required** (a separate test `.csproj` project) | `PascalCase.cs` |
| Python | `src/<package>/` | Unit tests beside the code files (`test_*.py`) · integration and e2e in `tests/` | `snake_case.py` |
| Dart / Flutter | `lib/` | `test/` · `integration_test/` **required** (same layout as `lib/`) | `snake_case.dart` (lint `file_names`) · `android/` `ios/` stay in the repo |

When another skill writes `tests/` or `test/`, read it as "the test folder of that stack". Pick one name and use it across the whole repo.


## reference: readme-by-stack.md

# README by language — commands, files and extra sections

Use this with [`readme-skeleton.md`](readme-skeleton.md). These tables are a fallback and a starting point for search terms (`SKILL.md` item 2, layer 2). They are not commands you can paste in as is. Take the real commands from the project's files and the official documentation for the version in use. **Run every command on a clean machine before it goes into the README** (`SKILL.md` item 2). A cell marked ※ means the official page was not opened to confirm it in the round it was written (2026-11-07).

## 1 · Versions, main files and per-environment settings

Put these into README section 4 "Prerequisites" and section 6 "Configuration".

| Stack | manifest + lock (commit both) | Pin the runtime version in a file | Per-environment settings |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node / TypeScript | `package.json` + `package-lock.json` or `pnpm-lock.yaml` (one lock type only) | `.nvmrc` (`nvm use`) · `engines` in `package.json` is only a warning until `engine-strict` is on | Vite: `.env` · `.env.[mode]` · `.env.local` · only `VITE_*` reaches the browser · Angular: `src/environments/` + `ng build --configuration <name>` |
| .NET / C# | `.sln` or `.slnx` + `.csproj` · `packages.lock.json` optional ※ | `global.json` → `sdk.version` (full number) + `rollForward` (set `disable` when using a lock file) | `appsettings.json` + `appsettings.{Env}.json` · chosen by `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` (web) or `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT` · unset = Production · dev secrets: `dotnet user-secrets` · `launchSettings.json` is for dev machines only |
| Python | `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` · do not commit `.venv` | `.python-version` (`uv python pin`) + `requires-python` | No central standard · `.env` + environment variables, or the framework's settings ※ |
| Java / Kotlin | `pom.xml` or `build.gradle.kts` + `settings.gradle.kts` | Gradle wrapper (commit `gradlew` `gradlew.bat` `gradle/wrapper/*`) · Maven wrapper `mvnw` ※ · Java Development Kit (JDK) version | Spring Boot: `application.yml` + `application-{profile}.yml` · enable with `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE` or `--spring.profiles.active=prod` |
| Go | `go.mod` + `go.sum` | The `go 1.xx` line (minimum) + `toolchain` | No standard · environment variables ※ |
| Flutter / Dart | `pubspec.yaml` + `pubspec.lock` (apps commit the lock · libraries do not) | `environment:` in pubspec ※ · FVM if used (not official) | Flavors: Android `productFlavors` in `android/app/build.gradle.kts` · iOS uses schemes ※ · `--dart-define` ※ |
| Rust | `Cargo.toml` + `Cargo.lock` | `rust-toolchain.toml` (`channel` + `components`) | No standard · environment variables ※ |
| PHP / Laravel | `composer.json` + `composer.lock` | `"php": "^8.x"` in `require` | `.env` (not committed) + `.env.example` · `APP_ENV` selects `.env.[APP_ENV]` · `APP_DEBUG=false` in production |

## 2 · Commands

Put these into README section 5 "Getting started", 7 "Common commands" and 10 "Build and output files".

| Stack | Install | Run | test | lint · format | build / package → output files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Node / TypeScript | `npm ci` (follows the lock) · `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` | `npm run dev` ※ | `npm test` ※ | `npm run lint` ※ · Prettier ※ | `npm run build` ※ → `dist/` |
| .NET / C# | `dotnet restore` | `dotnet run` · `dotnet run -lp https` | `dotnet test` ※ | `dotnet format` ※ | `dotnet publish` (net8.0 and later default to Release) → `bin/Release/<tfm>/publish/` · `-r <RID> --self-contained` (Runtime Identifier (RID), for example `linux-x64`) |
| Python | `uv sync` | `uv run <command>` | `uv run pytest` ※ | `ruff check` · `ruff format` | `uv build` ※ → wheel · sdist |
| Java / Kotlin | Fetched at build time | `./mvnw spring-boot:run` · `./gradlew bootRun` ※ | `./mvnw test` · `./gradlew test` ※ | Spotless · Checkstyle · ktlint (no single standard) ※ | `./mvnw package` · `./gradlew build` ※ → a jar, run with `java -jar` |
| Go | `go mod download` ※ | `go run ./cmd/<name>` ※ | `go test ./...` ※ | `gofmt` · `go vet` ※ | `go build ./...` ※ → one binary file |
| Flutter / Dart | `flutter pub get` ※ | `flutter run --flavor <name>` | `flutter test` ※ | `flutter analyze` · `dart format .` ※ | `flutter build appbundle` → `build/app/outputs/bundle/release/app.aab` · `flutter build ipa` ※ |
| Rust | `cargo fetch` ※ | `cargo run` ※ | `cargo test` ※ | `cargo clippy` · `cargo fmt` ※ | `cargo build --release` ※ → `target/release/` |
| PHP / Laravel | `composer install` · `npm ci && npm run build` (assets) ※ | `php artisan serve` ※ | `php artisan test` | Laravel Pint ※ | deploy: `php artisan config:cache` (never run in dev) · `php artisan storage:link` |

## 3 · Extra README sections by language

| Stack | What to add |
|---|---|
| Node / TypeScript | The Node version from `.nvmrc` + tell readers to run `nvm use` · npm or pnpm (never 2 lock types) · a `scripts` table · every `VITE_*` variable, with a warning that the value reaches the browser · Angular: the list of configurations |
| .NET / C# | The Software Development Kit (SDK) version from `global.json` · which project is the startup project · where `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` is set · the key names to set through `user-secrets` (no values) · the `dotnet publish` command actually used · the EF Core migration commands |
| Python | The version from `.python-version` · uv, or venv + pip (one way only) · with a src layout, install before testing · where the ruff settings live · the `.env` file that must exist |
| Java / Kotlin | The JDK version · always use `./mvnw` or `./gradlew`, never the locally installed tool · a profile table and how to enable each · the name and location of the jar produced |
| Go | The version from the `go` and `toolchain` lines · what each binary in `cmd/` does · the environment variables read |
| Flutter / Dart | The Flutter and Dart versions · a flavor table (name · applicationId · entry file) · signing: where `key.properties` and the keystore are, and whom to ask (never commit them) · iOS: team and provisioning · the build command per flavor and where the output lands |
| Rust | The toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml` · the feature flags available · the binaries in `src/bin/` · the Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) if it is a library |
| PHP / Laravel | The PHP version and required extensions · `cp .env.example .env` → `php artisan key:generate` ※ → migrate · build assets · deploy steps (`config:cache` · `storage:link` · queue worker) |

## 4 · Folder layout from official sources

Use this for README section 8 "Project structure". This repo's rules (code folder name · test location) are in `SKILL.md` item 1 and win when they conflict.

| Stack | Layout the tools expect | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Node / TypeScript | npm sets none · follow the framework generator (`src/` · `public/` · `vite.config.ts` or `angular.json`) ※ | — |
| .NET / C# | No official page · most common is `src/<App>/` + `tests/<App>.Tests/` + `global.json` + `.slnx` ※ | — |
| Python | src layout: `src/<package>/` · `pyproject.toml` at the root | [PyPA src vs flat](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/src-layout-vs-flat-layout/) |
| Java / Kotlin | `src/main/java` (or `kotlin`) · `src/main/resources` · `src/test/java` | [Maven Standard Directory Layout](https://maven.apache.org/guides/introduction/introduction-to-the-standard-directory-layout.html) |
| Go | `cmd/<binary>/main.go` · `internal/` · a small package can keep its files at the root · `golang-standards/project-layout` and `pkg/` come from the community, not the Go team | [Organizing a Go module](https://go.dev/doc/modules/layout) |
| Flutter / Dart | `lib/` (`lib/src/` for internals) · `test/` · `android/` · `ios/` ※ | [Dart package layout](https://dart.dev/tools/pub/package-layout) |
| Rust | `src/main.rs` · `src/lib.rs` · `src/bin/` · `tests/` · `examples/` · `benches/` | [Cargo project layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/project-layout.html) |
| PHP / Laravel | `app/` · `config/` · `database/` · `public/` · `resources/` · `routes/` · `storage/` · `tests/` | [Laravel 13.x structure](https://laravel.com/docs/13.x/structure) |

[npm ci](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/commands/npm-ci) · [package.json engines](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v10/configuring-npm/package-json) · [pnpm install](https://pnpm.io/cli/install) · [nvm .nvmrc](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm/blob/master/README.md) · [Vite env and mode](https://vite.dev/guide/env-and-mode) · [Angular environments](https://angular.dev/tools/cli/environments) · [global.json](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/global-json) · [ASP.NET Core environments](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/environments) · [user-secrets](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/security/app-secrets) · [dotnet publish](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-publish) · [Writing pyproject.toml](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/writing-pyproject-toml/) · [uv project layout](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/layout/) · [uv Python versions](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/python-versions/) · [Ruff configuration](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/configuration/) · [Gradle Wrapper](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/gradle_wrapper.html) · [Spring Boot profiles](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/reference/features/profiles.html) · [Spring Boot Maven run](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/maven-plugin/run.html) · [Go toolchains](https://go.dev/doc/toolchain) · [Flutter flavors](https://docs.flutter.dev/deployment/flavors) · [Flutter Android release](https://docs.flutter.dev/deployment/android) · [Cargo FAQ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/faq.html) · [rust-toolchain.toml](https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/overrides.html) · [Composer basic usage](https://getcomposer.org/doc/01-basic-usage.md) · [Laravel configuration](https://laravel.com/docs/12.x/configuration)

## reference: readme-skeleton.md

# README skeleton and companion documents — full version

The rules are in `SKILL.md` item 2 · a copy-ready template is in `assets/starter-files.md` · commands and files for each language are in [`readme-by-stack.md`](readme-by-stack.md)

## 1 · README sections in the order a newcomer needs them

> This table is the fallback and the length criteria for layer 3 in `SKILL.md` item 2 · the real sections of each project come from the layer 2 survey (read the project · official docs · READMEs of projects of the same type) · a section that this type of project needs but that is not in the table may be added.

The order follows what someone who has just arrived needs: what is this → install → run → change code → ship · the "Sources" column is the number of the 5 main sources (item 4) that recommend the section · a row that merges several topics gives a range · "—" means no main source recommends it; it is this skill's own judgment. The section names in the "Section" column are the Thai headings written into the README, so they stay Thai (English gloss in brackets).

| # | Section | Question it answers | Present when | How long · where to move it if longer | Sources |
|:--:|---|---|---|---|:--:|
| 1 | ชื่อ + ทำอะไรให้ใคร (name + what it does for whom) | What is this, who uses it | always | 2–3 lines · first line at most 120 characters | 5 |
| 2 | บรรทัดสถานะ (status line) | Is it still in development, who owns it, where are the docs | always | 1 line: status · owner · link to `docs/README.md` | 2–4 (status 2 · owner 4 · docs link 4) |
| 3 | ภาพหน้าจอหรือตัวอย่างผล (screenshot or sample output) | What does it look like or produce | there is a screen or output to look at | 1 image, or a sample command with its output | 2 (usage example 3) |
| 4 | ต้องมีบนเครื่อง (needed on the machine) | What must be installed first, which version | always | table: tool · version · which file pins the version (`.nvmrc` · `global.json`) | 3 |
| 5 | เริ่มใช้งาน (getting started) | How to install and run | always | commands that can be copied, pasted and run, at most 6 commands · more than that becomes `scripts/setup` | 4 |
| 6 | ตั้งค่า (configuration) | What must be configured, how many environments, how to switch | the project reads values from outside | table: variable name · what it is for · required or not · sample value (no real values) · for a secret give only the name and where to get it · if there is none, write "ไม่มีค่าตั้งภายนอก" (no external config) | 0 · based on Twelve-Factor |
| 7 | คำสั่งที่ใช้บ่อย (common commands) | How to run dev · test · lint · format · build | always | table of 4–8 rows · test must be 1 command | 2 |
| 8 | โครงโปรเจกต์ (project layout) | What is in which folder | always | a one-level tree, at most 15 lines · more → `ARCHITECTURE.md`, code-map section | 1 |
| 9 | สถาปัตยกรรมย่อ (short architecture) | How many parts the system has, how they talk | more than 1 part (web page + API + database · queue · external service) | 3–5 lines + a Mermaid diagram at Context or Container level · full → `ARCHITECTURE.md` | — · based on matklad and C4 |
| 10 | build และไฟล์ที่ได้ (build and output files) | How to make the deliverable, what files come out, where | there is something to build (web · app · binary · package) | build command per target + the path of the output file | 2 (counted together with deploy) |
| 11 | deploy | Where it goes live, who triggers it, through which Continuous Integration (CI), how to roll back | it can be deployed | 3–5 lines · full steps → `docs/runbook-deploy.md` | 2 (counted together with build) |
| 12 | ติดปัญหา (troubleshooting) | Common symptoms and fixes | always | table of symptom · fix · start from what you hit yourself while writing the README | — |
| 13 | ร่วมพัฒนา (contributing) | branch · commit · pull request (PR) · what to check before sending | other people change the code | 3–5 lines · longer → `CONTRIBUTING.md` | 4 |
| 14 | ติดต่อและขอความช่วยเหลือ (contact and help) | Whom to ask when stuck, which channel | always | 1–2 lines | 4 |
| 15 | สัญญาอนุญาต (license) | How far it can be reused | always · the last section | 1 line + the `LICENSE` file · for internal work write "ใช้ภายใน <บริษัท> ห้ามเผยแพร่" (internal use at <company>, do not distribute) | 2 |

**Skeleton rules**
- Cut a section that has nothing in it; do not write "none" · except section 6, which must say there is no external config.
- The README holds only what a newcomer needs in the first 30 minutes · anything longer moves to the file named in column 2, with a link back; do not delete it.
- Longer than 100 lines → put a table of contents under the status line.
- Edit the README in the same commit as the code that changes a command or setting.
- Each language has sections to add (Flutter flavors · .NET `user-secrets`) → [`readme-by-stack.md`](readme-by-stack.md) section 3.

## 2 · What goes into other files

| File | Lives at | Content | Create when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ARCHITECTURE.md` | `<project-name>/` | a code map for people who change the code (section 3) | the folder tree in the README exceeds 15 lines, or the system has more than 1 part |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | `<project-name>/` | what users see changing in each version | per the table in `SKILL.md` item 3 |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | `<project-name>/` | developer machine setup · branch · commit · PR · lint and test before sending | README section 13 is longer than 5 lines |
| `LICENSE` | `<project-name>/` | the full license text | the repo is public, or the contract requires it |
| `SECURITY.md` | `<project-name>/` or `.github/` | how to report a vulnerability · versions still supported | the repo is public, or delivered to a customer who maintains it |
| `CODEOWNERS` | `.github/` | which folder whom must review in a PR | there are several teams or owners |
| `runbook-deploy.md` | `docs/` at the root | build → release → run steps · each environment's setup · rolling back | the deploy steps are longer than 5 lines |
| `decisions/ADR-NNNN-<slug>.md` | `docs/` at the root | decision records (Architecture Decision Record (ADR)), one per decision | a hard-to-reverse decision is made (`adr-writer`) |
| Architecture, delivery edition | `docs/` at the root | an arc42-style architecture document | delivering to a customer or there is an acceptance reviewer (`project-doc-set`) |

The location of `docs/` follows layout B in `project-doc-set` item 1 · GitHub looks for `CONTRIBUTING` and `CODEOWNERS` in `.github/` first, then the repo root, then `docs/` · documents in `docs/` can be split by what the reader needs into 4 kinds (Diátaxis): learning (tutorial) · getting a job done (how-to, e.g. a runbook) · looking up facts (reference, e.g. an API settings table) · understanding the reasons (explanation, e.g. ARCHITECTURE · ADR)

## 3 · ARCHITECTURE.md

**Default: matklad's short form** — the reader is someone who will change the code and wants to know where the thing that does X lives.

```markdown
# สถาปัตยกรรม

## ภาพรวม
<ระบบแก้ปัญหาอะไร รับอะไรเข้า ส่งอะไรออก — 1 ย่อหน้า + รูป Context หรือ Container 1 รูป>

## แผนที่โค้ด
<แต่ละโฟลเดอร์หรือโมดูลหลักทำอะไร คุยกับใคร — ทีละย่อหน้าสั้น ๆ>

## ข้อห้ามที่ต้องรักษา
```

- Short; include only what rarely changes · you may name a file, module or type, but put no links, because links break when files move; let people search by name instead.
- Do not explain every module in detail · do not chase every commit · review 2–3 times a year.

# skill: no-ai-look

Use when making visuals so they do not look AI-made

# no-ai-look — work that looks designed by a person, not by AI

> **One rule:** every choice (color, font, layout, image, word) must be answerable as "chosen because of this project", not "because it is the default."

**Last line of every answer that makes or reviews a visual piece, including a quick "is it OK to send?" check:** the `no-ai-look:` line from 3.3, with real counts (eye check `ด่านตา n/9`, web pages add `(หน้าเว็บ n/14)`). Items you could not check count as not passed. A script result of 0 never makes the line pass. Script not run (no shell) → write `สคริปต์ ไม่ได้รัน` in its slot. If the `ด่านก่อนลงมือ:` line of `design-references` is also due, put it right above this one.

## Use when
- Making or reviewing any visual: web page, slide, poster, post, image, logo, document cover, diagram.
- Asked "is this OK to send?" for such work.

Not for: spacing, color system, fonts and components → the job's own skill (`ui-craft` · `presentation-design` · `graphic-design` · `brand-kit` · `brief-to-image` · `image-generation`). Words in the work → `human-writing`.

**A look the project already approved wins** (brand kit · diagram house style · delivered theme). If it matches a ban below, keep it and note it as intentional.

## 1 · Before starting — decide 5 things and write them where the project keeps its look
(`docs/README.md` field `doc-theme` · app tokens · brand kit; create no new file if a place exists.)

1. **What the work is for**, choose 1: persuade · use · read · experience. Layout comes from this. Sketch 2–3 really different layouts in ASCII, pick one with a 1-line reason; the first idea is usually the default.
2. **1 main color** tied to this business; derive neutrals from it. Never a framework default as the brand color (Tailwind indigo-500 `#6366f1` · shadcn/ui default dark gray button).
3. **2 fonts**: 1 heading font with personality + 1 easy body font, 1-line reason each. Thai work needs full Thai coverage.
4. **A real source of inspiration**: the product's own world or a named style (Swiss · risograph · 1960s travel posters), never floating adjectives ("พรีเมียม" "ทันสมัย"). Search references first with `design-references` (plugin `superuser`), then extract colors from the chosen work. Use the stored color library only when live search is impossible.
5. **Real content**: names, numbers, dates, real screenshots. If missing, put `(รอยืนยัน)`; never invent.

**Test:** remove the logo. If a competitor could still use the work, add what only this project has.

## 2 · Common signals — never the default
Each is allowed if the project gives a reason. The fix for every signal and the sources: the catalog.

- **Color/surface:** purple-blue-cyan gradient · gradient text · neon on dark · glow circle · frosted glass across the page · decorative grid or stripes · cream + terracotta + serif set · line + wide shadow on one box → 1 solid brand color; emphasis by size or weight.
- **Cards/headings:** colored side bar on a rounded card · cards in cards · blob radius · grid of 3–6 identical cards · small badge or icon tile above a heading · 01/02/03 with no real sequence · giant italic serif · Inter/Geist everywhere → spacing and type; group by importance.
- **Page structure:** hero → 3 cards → logos → pricing → FAQ · opening → feature list → how it works → install button · giant number + small label in 3 boxes · every slide title + 3–4 bullets → structure from the page's goal.
- **Icons/motion:** emoji as icons · one thin-line set at 16 everywhere · fade-up on everything · blinking dot or cursor · self-scrolling · bouncy easing · zoom on hover → one chosen SVG set; move only what has meaning, 150–300 ms ease-out, transform/opacity.
- **AI images:** plastic skin · golden or dramatic light everywhere · teal-orange · too-clean scene · average people · bad hands, teeth, text · clay 3D or glossy isometric → one reasoned light source, signs of use, edit the result.
- **Logos:** gradient circle with a hole · circuits · infinity · swoosh · melting letters → shape from something specific; vector; test at favicon size.
- **Documents:** emoji before headings · every bullet starts bold · Title Case everywhere · every section a list · 4 heading levels in a short note · summary ending every section · default Mermaid → short prose, house-style diagrams.
- **Words:** broad ad words (supercharge · ยกระดับ · ไร้รอยต่อ) · "ไม่ใช่แค่ X แต่คือ Y" · sets of 3 · many long dashes · canned openers ("ในยุคดิจิทัลที่…") → `human-writing`, `thai-grammar`.

Do not swap one default for another (cream + terracotta + serif, or + olive, is still a formula). Bento grids and mesh gradients are not signals in themselves. A multi-hue gradient built from the brand hue and its neighbours, on 1 focal place and never on text, is the owner's taste, not the `ai-palette` signal (rules in `design-references` `references/depth-and-light.md` section 3b, 2026-11-24).

When the owner's theme asks for depth (`มีมิติ` · `แสงเงา` · `ลูกเล่น`), soft shadows, one glow and glass over photos are the reason, not a signal, as long as the piece stays inside the limits in `design-references` `references/depth-and-light.md` section 4. The eye checker judges against those limits: 3 layers at most, one light direction, flat text, glow on 1 item.

## 3 · Check before sending

### 3.1 HTML/CSS work (mockup · web page · HTML deck · HTML cover)

```bash
python <path ของ skill นี้>/scripts/slop_scan.py <ไฟล์หรือโฟลเดอร์>          # ตาราง
python <path ของ skill นี้>/scripts/slop_scan.py <path> --min P2 --json       # เฉพาะข้อหนัก
python <path ของ skill นี้>/scripts/slop_scan.py --url https://...           # หน้าที่ขึ้นเว็บแล้ว + stylesheet ที่หน้า <link> ไว้ (ไม่รัน JavaScript) · path ไฟล์ในเครื่องหรือ file:///... ก็ได้
python <path ของ skill นี้>/scripts/slop_scan.py --self-test                  # รันก่อน ถ้าแก้สคริปต์
```

- The `ui-scan` hook runs this on every Write/Edit of a UI file (P0/P1 sent back to fix at once; off with `"ui_scan": false` in `.claude/superuser/config.json`). It checks one file at a time, so before sending still run the whole folder once.
- Page drawn entirely by JavaScript: `--url` sees only the skeleton → check the source, or save the page as .html and scan that.
- 43 rules from the code; nothing to install. Levels: P0 unusable · P1 hard to read · P2 clear AI signal · P3 look again (may be intentional). Any P0 or P1 → exit 1; 0 files checked → exit 2 (wrong, not a pass).
- Fix P0/P1 first, then P2. For intentional items write `/* slop-ok: <rule> <reason> */` or `<!-- slop-ok: <rule> <reason> -->` in that file.
- A script result is a reason to look again, not an order. It cannot see images, and it catches only defaults readable from code. **0 items is not a pass**: send only after both the script and the eye gate 3.2 pass.

### 3.2 Eye gate (every medium: images, slides, posters, Word documents)

Render to an image at real size and answer each item yes or no, by the criterion in the item (for some, "yes" means fail). An item with several questions passes only if every question passes. For a failed item, fix it, or give the reason it is kept under `## ตัดสินใจเอง`.

1. **Logo and product name covered, can you still tell whose it is?** No = fail. Also swap in a competitor's name: if every sentence and image is still true = fail.
2. **Squint:** one dominant element, or everything shouting at once?
3. **Count the item-2 signals:** 3 or more in one piece = looks AI-made. If the piece uses the depth exception (section 2, last paragraph), first answer the checks in `design-references` `references/depth-and-light.md` section 5 and write the result in the `no-ai-look:` field; only signals inside those limits are left out of the count, anything past them counts.
4. **Real content:** names, numbers, real images, or only generic words and stock photos?
5. **One set:** every slide or post uses one system, but the layout does not repeat on every page. A single piece answers `ไม่ใช้` and counts as passed.
6. **AI images:** check hands, teeth, text, shadows, light, real-world scale; zoom to 200% before use.
7. **Blank space:** room for the important things to breathe, not packed edge to edge?
8. **Words:** read headings aloud; a person telling a friend, or a slogan on a sign (slogan = fail)? Does a heading break mid-phrase (such as "ทำงานเป็น / ทีม")? Check web at width 375, slides/posts/covers at real size; if it breaks = fail, fix with `<wbr>` or `text-wrap: balance`. A heading the user worded themselves is used as given, noted as kept on purpose. **Large Thai type:** zoom on upper vowels and tone marks (ที่ · ทั้ง · ปี่) and lower vowels (ุ · ู); a collision with the neighbouring line = fail; raise line spacing per [`thai-line-breaking`](../human-writing/references/thai-line-breaking.md) (Thai headings no lower than 1.4).
9. **Cut 1 piece before sending:** find something removable without loss (shadow · border · decorative icon · label above a heading · motion · gradient · summary paragraph) and really remove it; send only if nothing is found. Do not cut shadows, rounded corners, the hero image, or icons that the look's depth language or the owner's style requires (flat-to-the-bone is the opposite mistake).

**Web pages, marketing landing pages and a product home page answer 5 more** (opening section = first screen before scrolling):

10. **Does the opening section have at least 1 real thing from the product** (screenshot of real use · real numbers with source · named real customer voice · real work done)? None = fail. At width 1440, unintended blank space over 1/3 of the screen = fail.
11. **Is the section order built on this product's story**, not the formula opening → features → how it works → install or pricing? Write 1 sentence on how this product's story is told (start from the user's problem · from a real demo · from customer results) and order by it. Keep the usual formula only if that sentence leads to the same order, and note it.
12. **Does a row of 3–6 equal cells have a reason from the content** (each really equally important and about equally long)? No reason = fail; enlarge the important cell or use a list, prose or one image. A sequence number on a cell heading is allowed only when the steps must be followed in order.
13. **Does the page color have a source other than the logo or icon** (a reference searched this round · the product's materials or world · an approved brand)? Pulled from the icon alone = fail.
14. **Is every mono font spot on code, commands, file names, or numbers that must align?** Mono on brand names, menus, table headers or captions to look "developer" = fail.

**Someone who did not make it must check by eye on every job before sending**; the maker cannot see their own defaults.
- Send the **rendered image at real size** (not code) to a fresh subagent: `design-critic` (graphic-design), else `reviewer`. Send 3.2 with the job's brief, never the maker's answer or opinion.
- Ask for the item-by-item answers of 3.2 and 3 places that look AI-made with fixes; no praise.
- Where reviewer and maker disagree, use the reviewer's answer, then fix or note why kept. After fixing, send the new image to a new reviewer for the fixed items only.
- A maker subagent that cannot call agents sends the image path back to the lead and writes `รอหัวหน้า` in the eye-check field.
- Skippable only for the reference board page and work the owner ordered skipped (the 3 directions sent to the owner at the end must still pass). If skipped, the result line says `ตรวจตา ข้าม เพราะ…`.

### 3.3 Record the result

1 line at the end: `no-ai-look: สคริปต์ P0 0 · P1 0 · P2 n (ตั้งใจ n) · ด่านตา 9/9 (หน้าเว็บ 14/14) · ตรวจตา <agent ที่ตรวจ> ไม่ตรงกับคนทำ n ข้อ · ตัดออก: <ชิ้นที่ตัด>`. An incomplete eye gate, or answers by the maker alone = not passed, even with 0 script items. Items kept on purpose go under `## ตัดสินใจเอง` with the reason. A new build also carries the `design-references` line `ด่านก่อนลงมือ:` with all 7 fields per its gate item 6.

## 4 · Brief for an image tool or a subagent task sheet

Always include, or you get the average:
- A named style + 1–3 real reference images (not adjectives).
- Brand hex colors · light source and time · lens or camera angle.
- Details observed from the real thing (place, signs of use, season, kind of people).
- What you do not want: teal-orange · plastic skin · golden light in every scene · text in the image (add text as a separate editable layer).
- **Edit** the first image you get (crop, retouch, adjust light); never use it as is.

## References
- [`references/catalog.md`](references/catalog.md) — open when the script reports an unfamiliar rule, for the fix and sources of any signal, or when checking media the script cannot see.


## reference: catalog.md

# catalog — signals that make work look AI-made (full version)

Extension of `no-ai-look`. Open it when the script reports an unfamiliar rule, or when you must check media the script cannot see.
The "Rule" column is the name in `scripts/slop_scan.py` (empty = checked by the eye gate, item 3.2). The "Source" column uses the codes in section 9. Only items with at least 2 sources are kept, except those marked (1 source).

## 1 · Colors and surfaces

| Signal | Why it looks AI | Use instead | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Purple-blue-cyan or pink gradient | Default from tutorials and frameworks; nobody chose it | 1 brand color tied to the business | `ai-palette` | IM · CM · UN · VP |
| Buttons and links in indigo `#6366f1` | Tailwind's indigo-500, often used by tutorials and AI-generated code (shadcn/ui's default is near-black dark gray, not indigo — checked 22 Oct 2026) | Set your own color tokens | `framework-default` | CM · UN · SK · VP · 21 |
| Gradient text | Decorative emphasis that says nothing | Solid color + size or weight | `gradient-text` | IM · DC |
| Neon/glow shadows on dark backgrounds | The default "cyberpunk" recipe | Reduce glow so the data stands out | `neon-glow` | IM · DC |
| A circular glow behind the content | The most common AI backdrop | Spacing, contrast, clear headings | `radial-halo` | IM · DC |
| Cream/beige background + serif + olive green | "Good taste" that became the new recipe | Choose from the project's context | `cream-palette` | IM · UN · SK |
| Cream background (about `#F4F1EA`) + terracotta accent + high-contrast serif headings as the starting set | The "warm, tasteful" set the model grabs when the brief fixes no colors. Terracotta is close to Anthropic's own brand color, so client work gives it away easily | Colors from the business and the project's real materials · cream is fine when the brand or brief orders it | `cream-palette` in part (catches the cream background, not the terracotta) | AN (1 source · anthropics/skills `frontend-design` Apache-2.0 · checked 2026-10-23) |
| Tinted black (`#111` · `#0B0B0B`) instead of black on every job, with 1 warm accent color as the default | A template's decorating habit applied whatever the subject; looks deliberate but nobody chose it | True black, or a dark shade of a brand color with a reason from the job · note the reason beside the token | | AN (1 source · the template chrome section of `frontend-design` · checked 2026-10-23) |
| Frosted glass across the whole page | Decoration; does not solve a layering problem | Use only for things that really float over content | `glassmorphism` | IM · DC |
| Decorative grid or stripe pattern on the background | Fills empty space with lines | Plain background · grid only for canvas/maps | `grid-bg` `stripes` | IM (1 source) |
| The whole shadcn default set (slate gray · one corner radius across the app · `rounded-2xl shadow-lg p-6` · `max-w-7xl`) | The look of a framework, not a decision | Set tokens for color, corners, shadow, spacing before building | `framework-default` in part | CM · UN · SK · VP · CV |
| Both low contrast and gray on a colored background | Looks "clean" but cannot be read | ≥ 4.5:1 · use a dark shade of the background color | `low-contrast` | IM (1 source) |

## 2 · Cards, boxes and page structure

| Signal | Why it looks AI | Use instead | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A thick colored bar on the side of a rounded card | Makes an ordinary card look like a warning | Remove it if it does not show status · a solid-color label | `side-tab` | IM · GD (item 7) |
| Cards inside cards | Too deep; little room left to work | Spacing, type, divider lines | `nested-cards` | IM (1 source) |
| A 1px line + wide shadow on one box | Defines the edge twice | Choose one | `hairline-shadow` | IM (1 source) |
| Corner radius too big for the box | Every card is the same blob | Reduce by box size | `huge-radius` | IM (1 source) |
| A grid of identical icon-heading-text cards | Every item has the same weight | Group · make the important item bigger | | IM · GD |
| Giant number + small label + 3-box stats | A sales-page template | Use numbers when they help explain, with context | | IM (1 source) |
| Fixed page structure: centered hero → 3 cards → customer logos → pricing → FAQ → 4-column footer | The order of a template, not of the page | Build from the page's goal and what the reader must do first | | CM · UN · VP · SK |
| Identical spacing everywhere | Cannot tell what is in the same group | Close within a group, far between groups | | IM (1 source) |
| Everything symmetric, everything centered | No point of intent | Asymmetry · 1 large cell · an off-center hero | | 21 · AN · GA |
| Settings content crammed in a modal | Not enough room | A separate page | | IM (1 source) |

## 3 · Type and headings

| Signal | Why it looks AI | Use instead | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Inter/Geist on every job | Makes different products look the same | A font by personality · keep it if it is the brand font | `overused-font` | IM · GD · AN |
| Switching to Space Grotesk on every job instead | The new default | A reason from the project | | UN · SK |
| Giant italic serif | A shortcut to "editorial" | A typeface by the product's personality | `italic-serif-display` | IM (1 source) |
| A small badge above the heading ("Introducing" · "New") | Adds a line that says nothing and looks clickable | Put that word in the heading, or cut it | `eyebrow-badge` | IM (1 source) |
| An icon in a rounded tile above a card heading | The AI feature-card pattern | An icon beside the heading, or remove the tile | `icon-tile` | IM (1 source) |
| Numbers 01/02/03 with no sequence | Clutter that says nothing | Use when there are real steps | `numbered-labels` | IM (1 source) |
| A long display-size heading eating the first screen | No room left to explain | Shorter or smaller | | IM (1 source) |
| Heading and body at close sizes | Cannot be scanned | Clear difference in size, weight, spacing | | IM (1 source) |
| Strongly squeezed letter spacing | Letters touch and are hard to read | Not below -0.03em | `crushed-tracking` | IM (1 source) |
| Emoji in headings or in place of icons | No icon system | One SVG set | `emoji-heading` | CM · UN · WW |
| One thin-line icon set (such as Lucide) at size 16 everywhere | Repeats across every product | Choose a set on purpose · use real screenshots/charts instead | | BL · 2S |

## 4 · Motion

| Signal | Use instead | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| fade-up and hover-scale on every piece | Move only what has meaning, 150–300 ms ease-out · a site that must feel alive uses 4 entrance styles in turn, not the same one everywhere (`dynamic-website` in software-development) | | UN · SK · BL |
| A status dot that blinks nonstop | Still · moves when the status changes | `pulsing-dot` | IM (1 source) |
| A blinking cursor in still text | Keep it in typeable fields | `blinking-cursor` | IM (1 source) |
| Text/logos that scroll by themselves | Still, or with a stop button | `marquee` | IM (1 source) |
| Bouncy or stretchy easing | Settle fast · bounce only where it fits the product | `bounce-easing` | IM · GD motion-basics |
| Animating width, spacing, or `transition: all` | transform/opacity | `layout-animation` | IM (1 source) |
| An image that zooms or rotates on hover | Still, unless it says it can be clicked | `hover-zoom-image` | IM (1 source) |
| Content hidden waiting for an animation, and if the script fails it never appears | Visible by default | | IM (1 source) |

## 5 · Words on screens, slides and ads

The main principles are in `human-writing` item 3. This table keeps only what shows up in design work.

| Signal | Use instead | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Broad ad words (supercharge · world-class · seamless · ยกระดับ · ไร้รอยต่อ · ล้ำสมัย) | Say what the user can do and how much better | `buzzword` | IM · WW · 2S |
| "Not a feature. A platform." · "ไม่ใช่แค่… แต่คือ…" | Explain directly | `forced-contrast` | IM · human-writing |
| A long dash in every sentence | English: split into sentences with a full stop · Thai: a space or a new paragraph, no full stop mid-paragraph (`thai-grammar` `f3` `t-dash`) | `em-dash-overuse` | IM · WW |
| Canned opening sentences ("In today's fast-paced world" · "ในยุคดิจิทัลที่…") | Open with what only this product can do | `stock-opener` | 2S · WW |
| Short fragments split by full stops ("Fast. Simple. Powerful.") · sets of 3 · feature names of 2 nouns | A full sentence that carries information | | SJ · CM · WW · OW |
| No names, numbers or dates · claims a competitor could also make | 1 claim only we have, with a number | | 21 · GA · CP |
| Fake proof: a team photo that is not the team · logos that are not clients · invented personas | Real people, real clients only | | 21 · WW · CP |
| Emoji lined up in a promo line | None, or 1 that means something | | WW · CM |
| "theater" used to wave things off | Say what does not work and why | `theater` | IM (1 source) |
| Overly formal words (utilize · facilitate) · stiff connectors (Moreover) · hedges ("It's important to note") | Ordinary words | `stock-opener` in part | WW · TS |
| Thai: wrong register · ครับ/ค่ะ/pronouns that do not fit the reader · literal-translation idioms · English word order · cutting words until curt | Read aloud · register from the table in `human-writing` `references/thai-grammar.md` section 4 · sentence structure per sections 1–2 of the same file · run `scripts/thai_tells.py` of `human-writing` | | 1S · `thai-grammar` |

## 6 · AI images, logos, posters, posts

| Signal | Use instead | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Smooth pore-free skin · every material glossy in the same way | Keep real texture and marks | KR · BK · MF |
| Saturated color, golden or dramatic light in every scene, even indoors | One light source with a reason, matching shadows | BK · GC · KR |
| Teal-orange tone (the shorter the prompt, the more it happens) | Specify the palette, or order it away | FL · 2S |
| Average-looking, perfect, stereotyped people | Details from observation: place, time, what kind of people | BK · KR · CP |
| A showroom-clean scene | Wrinkles, signs of use, ordinary light | MF · KR |
| Wrong physics: shadows not matching light, wrong reflections, bent lines, unrealistic scale | Check by eye before use | KR · MF |
| Hands, teeth, garbled text, crowds with repeated faces | Zoom to 200% to check · put text in a separate layer | KR · FL · MR |
| Using the first image you get without editing | Crop, edit, adjust (1 source, but matches the principle "edit, do not just accept") | CP |
| Clay 3D / isometric / glossy | A style that fits the brand · real photos | 2S · MF · branded-document-design `cover-design.md` item 9 |
| Prompting with adjectives ("premium" · "vibrant") | A named style + reference image + hex | MR · VP · CP |
| A gradient circle logo with a hole in the middle · swoosh curves · infinity · circuit patterns | A shape from something specific (DeepSeek's whale · Midjourney's sailboat) | QW · BU |
| Letters that are almost letters, melting, off symmetry, details lost at small size, raster file only | Vector · test at favicon size · real lettering | BU · KR · MR |
| A poster packed edge to edge, no blank space, tiny paragraphs | 1 hero item · lots of white space · cut words so the key word can be big | MR · KR |
| Many fonts and many image styles in one frame (flat + realistic 3D + textured lettering) | 2–3 fonts, one visual language | MR · KR |
| Text embedded in the image | An editable text layer | KR · MR |
| A feed where each post has a different style | One brand system across every post | KR · PN · 2S |
| Floating glowing circles meaning "technology" · stock photos of handshakes · arrows shooting up | The real thing, or empty space | GD (item 7) (1 source) |

## 7 · Slides, documents, diagrams

| Signal | Use instead | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Every slide has one layout with 3–4 bullets of equal length | Change with the content · have some one-sentence pages | | 2S · GA |
| One title pattern across slides (equal length · Title Case · with a colon) | Title = the conclusion (`human-writing` item 6) | | 2S · TS |
| Line icons and middling images that fit any topic | Real photos, charts, screenshots | | 2S · GA |
| No real data, client details or brand | Put in real data, or `(รอยืนยัน)` | | GA · 21 |
| Every bullet starts in bold | Prose, or a plain list | `bold-first-bullets` | TF · TS |
| Emoji before headings · lots of bold · odd bullet symbols | Plain headings · bold in 2–3 places | `emoji-heading` | TS · WW · 2S |
| Over-formatting: lists everywhere, 4 levels of headings, tables in a short note | Merge sections, cut headings | | TS · UM |
| Ending every section with a summary or opinion | End when it has all been said | | TS · WW |
| References or components that do not exist (dead links · fake DOIs · services the system does not have) | Check every one against the source or code | | TS · IL |
| Default-looking Mermaid: self-placed, tangled arrows with no labels, several flows in one picture | The project's house style · a label on every arrow · 1 flow per picture | | YM · IL |
| Lorem text or "ตัวอย่าง" | Realistic content | `lorem` | IM · ui-craft |

## 8 · Basic quality

Not AI signals directly, but really broken, and the script checks them: an input with only a placeholder (`placeholder-label`) · an image with no src (`broken-image`) · a skipped heading level (`skipped-heading`) · text under 11 px (`tiny-text`) · body line spacing under 1.3 (`tight-leading`) · justified alignment (`justified`) · letter-spaced body text (`wide-body-tracking`) · an all-caps paragraph (`all-caps-body`) · a nearly opaque color over an image (`image-overlay`)
Check only from the rendered page (the script cannot see): text overlapped · overflowing its frame · a menu cut off · lines longer than 75 characters · the first column of uneven length · JavaScript errors on load

**Not signals** (the data does not support them; do not hunt to cut): bento grid · mesh/blob gradient backgrounds (UN)
